title: Jude and the Clock
premise: In 1899 Prague, apprentice clockmaker Ulyana Blackwood is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, where she meets Jude, a disillusioned customs officer assigned to watch her. A sealed letter hidden in the clock's mechanism implicates her family in an anti-imperial plot, and Ulyana must smuggle the evidence past three city checkpoints before the century turns on New Year's Eve. Torn between duty and growing love for Jude, she chooses survival over silence, delivering the letter to a printer whose broadsheets force the conspirators' exposure. In the end, the master clock strikes midnight with Ulyana's name engraved inside its case—an inheritance she finally claims openly.
about_author: Sebastian Blackwood is the pen name of a former horologist's assistant who spent a decade restoring tower clocks across Central Europe before turning to fiction. His novels blend meticulous mechanical detail with quiet stories of people caught between empires.

chapters.title: The Summoning
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives at the observatory to repair the master clock, keeping her head down and her tools sharp. She notices a sealed letter wedged behind the escapement but leaves it untouched. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cautious anonymity, the comfort of work that asks no questions.

chapters.title: A Man Who Counts Seconds
chapters.summary: Jude, the customs officer assigned to observe all repairs, shadows Ulyana through the clock tower, suspicious of her family name. Their sparring over gears and regulations reveals unexpected mutual respect. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into fascination.

chapters.title: What the Escapement Kept
chapters.summary: Deep in the mechanism, Ulyana retrieves the sealed letter and discovers it names the Blackwoods in a conspiracy to sabotage the imperial mint. She hides it in her toolbag as Jude approaches. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread—the invisibility she built is already gone.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Ulyana maps her route out of the city: the river gate, the customs house, the New Year's cordon. Each checkpoint is manned by men who know her face or fear her name. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cold calculation replacing panic; survival becomes a design problem.

chapters.title: The River Gate
chapters.summary: First checkpoint: Ulyana sews the letter into a broken pendulum bob and passes the river gate among barge cargo, nearly caught when a guard weighs her bag. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into guilt—she has made Jude complicit by lying to him.

chapters.title: Confessions at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Jude confronts Ulyana with the discrepancy in her manifests. Instead of arresting her, he demands the truth, and she gives him half of it. He lets her go, breaking his own oath. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: love against duty—his first deliberate act of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Second checkpoint: Jude personally processes Ulyana's papers, falsifying a stamp while his superior watches. The conspirators, alerted by a leak, begin hunting the missing letter themselves. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness intertwined; there is no way back for either of them.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Belfry
chapters.summary: The conspirators ransack the observatory and take Ulyana's mentor hostage, demanding the letter by midnight. Ulyana realizes the third checkpoint—the New Year's cordon—is their trap. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into resolve; she will not trade another life for her safety.

chapters.title: Midnight Mechanism
chapters.summary: Climax: Ulyana walks into the cordon carrying a decoy letter while Jude smuggles the real one to the printer through the crowd's celebration. The conspirators seize the decoy just as the first broadsheets hit the streets. POV: alternating, converging at the tower steps. Emotional beat: sacrifice timed like a escapement—every second accounted for.

chapters.title: The Name Inside the Case
chapters.summary: The plot collapses; the mentor is freed, and the conspirators are arrested as church bells ring in 1900. Jude resigns his commission; Ulyana engraves both their names inside the restored master clock. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: resolution—inheritance reclaimed not as burden but as choice, love chosen over silence.
